The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Why, in plain words: Account pages started failing when a setting switched on a new monthly spending summary, and that summary likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 11m 39s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 42.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 8,265.67 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #575 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 15:47 UTC, not back to normal by 15:58:39 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 16:00:41 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 15:54:03 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 15:58:39 UTC - PR #575, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 15:47 UTC and was not back to normal by 15:58:39 UTC, at least 11 minutes 39 seconds later. 31.2% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 42.5% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 8,265.67 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Account pages started failing when a setting switched on a new monthly spending summary, and that summary likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #575, for a person to review and merge. Account page requests could go on failing with the division-by-zero error at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 while monthly-spend-feature stays on, and it was left on.

Impact
at least 11m 39s - since onset, still not back to normal
42.5% - peak error rate
4,494 - requests failed
0.9% to 31.2% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 8,265.67 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` sends the account page request to `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, which divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month that number is zero, so the request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and the account page fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of failed account page requests in the minute rose far above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 35 occurrences in 38 minutes, 15:17–15:54; # was 0.50% to 42.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 15:54
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 15 occurrences in 8 minutes, 15:47–15:54
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors started in the minute of the onset and were not seen before it.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at 15:47:53 UTC. Flag evaluations went from all off to all on starting in that minute, so account page requests began running the spend summary code path that the flag turns on.
  Evidence:
    P1 15:47:53 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 184 / on 16 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 15:47
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 15:48–15:54
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 15:48; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change. A rollout still under way: the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name.
      T7
      T8
      T9
    The service with the flag off: before the onset every evaluation read off, account pages rendered normally, and the error rate was typically low.
      G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 15:17–15:46
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 3 occurrences in 13 minutes, 15:26–15:38
      Gbac1
    Shoppers closing the connection: these ClientDisconnected failures were already being logged during the healthy stretch before the onset, while the error rate stayed typically low.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 41 occurrences in 36 minutes, 15:17–15:52
      Gbac1
why 3 The spend summary path divides by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for every evaluation at once. No staged rollout to a small share of traffic was seen. (AI-2)
- Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the code path it turns on for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. (AI-3)
- Nobody was paged: HighErrorRate on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 15:47:53 UTC. This enabled a spend summary code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and account page requests started failing. The error rate rose from about 1% to 30-40%. No deployment was involved. | 0.93 | refuted
C2 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 15:47:53 UTC. This enabled the spend summary code path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the account page error rate rose from about 1% to 30-40%. Argus's own switch-off at 15:54:14 UTC did not help, and Argus switched the flag back on at 15:57:03 UTC. | 0.85 | refuted, as tested for C1

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 15:54:15 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
 | 15:58:39 | Proposed a fix: PR #575 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 15:47 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 15:54 UTC, 7 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #575 | open
AI-2 | Make flag changes on io-shop roll out to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the account page error rate stays at its usual level. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Require a test that runs the code path an io-shop flag turns on, including for shoppers with no purchases this month, and have it pass before the flag can be switched on in production. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call engineer. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at io-shop that its flag evaluation log lines read off for every evaluation and that the ZeroDivisionError lines at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 stop. Keep it in place until the fault is fixed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Find out from io-shop's flag evaluation log lines after the switch-off whether the service read monthly-spend-feature as off. If it did, find out what else kept reaching the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and kept the account pages failing. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Before the Mitigation Agent judges a change it made, have it confirm from the service's own logs that the change reached the service. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 5 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 15:47.
- 14 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 15 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 4 minutes 39 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #575.
What went wrong
- Switching off the flag that the onset lines up with did not take the service off the incident's level. That left the incident with no mitigation, and the service was still failing when Argus escalated.
- The second investigation formed C2, which blames the same flag move that had just been tested and refuted, so it offered nothing new to try.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Supporting information

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item_this_month returned account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). It divides by however many purchases are flagged in_current_month. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has zero of those, so the function raised ZeroDivisionError. The incident evidence places that error at line 47. The test file calls this kind of shopper "the ordinary case". render_spend_summary sends the request to this function when use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false, which is the path monthly-spend-feature turns on.

The change: if nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0, meaning no spend per item this month. Otherwise it divides as before. The return type stays int.

Nothing is being silenced. No exception is caught; the empty month just gets the answer it should have. The lifetime figure, the typical-spend figure and the flag-off path in this file are untouched. That includes the existing test where a shopper with no history at all still raises through render_spend_summary with the flag off.

Tests added to tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py:
• One calls average_spend_per_item_this_month for a shopper with past purchases but none this month and expects 0. Against the old code this test would raise ZeroDivisionError.
• One calls render_spend_summary with use_monthly_summary=True for the same kind of shopper and expects 0. It covers the path the flag turns on.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist

○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  no candidate was confirmed - those tried were refuted
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, shoppers' account pages started failing after a setting switched on a new monthly spending summary. That summary likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but have bought nothing this month, because it divides by the number of this month's purchases. The problem lasted {duration}, and Argus estimates it cost the shop {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no on-call staff were called in. Argus turned the new setting back off, but that did not help, so the setting was switched on again. Argus has also proposed a fix. That fix is still a draft and has not been put in place.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
